newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power up slightly with BPA out.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power up slightly with BPA out.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S. rose slightly as the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) continued to hold off from offering next-day power during peak demand hours, trade sources said.
"BPA is still out of the market. Even though the weather is expected to warm up, prices are pretty firm," said one trader.
The federal power marketing agency, based in Portland, Ore., attributed the lack of surplus power to the continued outage of a 500 kilovolt transmission line in Washington state.
Due to voltage support concerns related to the line outage, power generation at hydroelectric dams has been curtailed.
Repairs to the line, which have been delayed by the weather and equipment needs, are expected to be finished Wednesday.
Also, the partial curtailment of the 1,158 megawatt (MW) nuclear unit in Washington state could end by Wednesday if a long-standing technical problem is solved, a spokesman said.
Restrictions on southbound transmissions on the AC segment of the Pacific Intertie were expected to end at 1800 PST, when maintenance work is scheduled to finish.

Forecasts called for temperatures in the Pacific Northwest to reach 6 to 12 degrees above normal by Thursday, while temperatures in the Southwest are expected to warm to 4 to 8 degrees above normal by the middle of the week.
Tuesday firm, peak electricity at the California-Oregon border (COB) was quoted at $15.50-16.50 per megawatt hour (MWh), compared with $14.00-16.00 for Monday.
Firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was quoted $13.50-15.00, while off-peak was at $7.50-9.00.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity was little changed at $16.00-17.00, while off-peak was quoted $7.50-9.00 per MWh.
Next-day firm, peak power at Four Corners was quoted $15.50-16.50, while off-peak was at $8.00-9.00.
COB for second-quarter delivery was last quoted $10.60-$10.90 per MWh, while second-quarter PV was quoted $14.35-$14.80, both up from Friday.
